question.text: The length of a metal wire is $L_{1}$ when the tension is $T_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ when the tension is $T_{2}$ The unstretched length of wire is

solution.text:
Let the initial length of the metal wire is $L$.
The strain at tension $T_{1}$ is $\Delta L_{1}=L_{1}-L$
The strain at tension $T_{2}$ is $\Delta L_{2}=L_{2}-L$
Suppose, the Young's modulus of the wire is $Y$, then
$\frac{\frac{T_{1}}{A}}{\frac{\Delta L_{1}}{L}}=\ rac{\frac{T_{2}}{A}}{\frac{\Delta L}{L}}$
where, $A$ is an cross-section of the wire assumed to be same at all the situations. $\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \frac{T_{1}}{A} \times \frac{L}{\Delta L_{1}} &=\frac{T_{2}}{A} \times \frac{L}{\Delta L_{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{T_{1}}{\left(L_{1}-L\right)} &=\frac{T_{2}}{\left(L_{2}-L\right)} \\ & T_{1}\left(L_{2}-L\right)=T_{2}\left(L_{1}-L\right) \cdot L=\frac{T_{2} L_{1}-T_{1} L_{2}}{T_{2}-T_{1}} \end{aligned}$
